claims.claim: Residents pay Bienes Personales on worldwide gross assets, with no deduction for debts (including a margin loan)

sources.name: PwC: Argentina, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 16 June 2026. Residents pay personal assets tax on worldwide assets as of 31 December "without consideration of liabilities"; FY2025 non-taxable threshold ARS 384,728,044.57; FY2025 general rates 0.50%, 0.75% and 1.00%; rates "gradually reduce to 0.25% by 2027". REIBP is open to individuals resident on 31 December 2023; the "good taxpayer" 0.50-point reduction for 2023–2025 is for those compliant for 2020–2022. No federal inheritance tax; the province of Buenos Aires "has gift and inheritance taxes based on certain conditions and amounts".

sources.name: Chambers: Private Wealth 2026, Argentina
sources.says: 2026 guide (cites Law 27.802 of March 2026). Residents pay PIT on worldwide income at progressive rates from 5% to 35%; Bienes Personales base is market value and "apart from a few exceptions" debts are not deductible; Law 27.743 sets 0.5% to 0.75% for 2026 and "a flat rate of 0.25%" for 2027. Only Buenos Aires Province levies a gift and inheritance tax (ITGB): PBA-domiciled persons on all assets received, others only on PBA-situs assets; no federal tax and none in the other provinces.

claims.note: localTaxes.ts (AR) models a gross base, and its note says the research did not say whether debts are deductible: PwC and Chambers now say they are not.

claims.claim: The $15M US exemption (2026) applies as anywhere

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Estate tax
sources.says: A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption, is more than the filing threshold for the year of death; the table gives 2026: $15,000,000. Page last reviewed or updated 23-Oct-2026.

sources.name: IRS news release IR-2025-103: tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026
sources.says: "Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000", up from $13,990,000 for 2025; the release (October 9, 2025) cites Revenue Procedure 2025-32 and is marked as an archival document.

sources.name: IRS: Some nonresidents with U.S. assets must file estate tax returns
sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. By contrast a nonresident who is not a citizen files when US-situated assets exceed $60,000. Page last reviewed or updated 27-Jun-2026.
